Separately, the majority of Comorian civil servants already receive salaries by wage transfer into bank accounts rather than in cash.

Uptake among smaller and informal merchants remains constrained by formal business-registration requirements.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Value=0 (unknown) because I did not find an official Comoros central bank/financial regulator consumer protection regulation or law specifically governing payment services (e.g., e-money consumer protection, dispute resolution, disclosure) beyond references that consumer protection is an objective of oversight and that Regulation 001/2017 includes “consumer protection issues”; I could not locate the text of Regulation 001/2017 or a dedicated consumer protection framework for payments in credible primary sources during this run.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A fast search located the actual Regulation 001/2017 text hosted on the BCC's own website plus the World Bank's oversight policy framework document describing it, which was authoritative enough to move the row to the full path. The World Bank document confirms BCC Regulation 001/2017 on electronic money sets out consumer protection and fund protection requirements, and that the 2019 Payment Law (Title II) requires fee transparency, disclosure of terms and dispute resolution for payment service users. These are payment-specific provisions, but they were reviewed via the World Bank's description rather than a full read of the primary legislative text, and enforcement/liability-allocation detail is unconfirmed, so a conservative Partial rating is applied. Recalculated from 0=Unknown to 2=Partial.
revised_comments: Comoros has payment-specific consumer protection provisions rather than a single dedicated, comprehensive framework. BCC Regulation 001/2017 governing electronic-money issuers includes consumer- and fund-protection requirements, and the 2019 Payment Law obliges payment service providers to ensure fee transparency, disclosure of terms and conditions, and dispute-resolution mechanisms, overseen by the Banque Centrale des Comores.
